Details.Education: BASIC EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS: Education must be accredited by an accrediting institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education in order for it to be credited towards qualifications (https://www.ed.gov/). Therefore, provide only the attendance and/or degrees from schools accredited by accrediting institutions recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. Failure to provide all of the required information as stated in this vacancy announcement may result in an ineligible rating or may affect the overall rating. Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: For 08XX series: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.orgOREvidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. For 1550 Series: Bachelor's degree in computer science or bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the DS-03 pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate some or all of the following: 1) Implementing information assurance policies; 2) Performing Risk Management Framework tasking and creating authorization packages; 3) Implementing cybersecurity programs; 4) Demonstrating experience and familiarity with the Joint Special Access Program Implementation Guide; and 5) Creating Concept of Operation (CONOPS), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M), System Security Plan (SSP), Security Controls Traceability Matrix (SCTM). Your experience must reflect skill in the following areas: attention to detail, customer service, oral communication, and problem solving. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/2200/information-technology-it-management-series-2210-alternative-a/ Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

MajorDuties: You will perform as the lead technical authority for all facets of Cybersecurity providing guidance and oversight on cybersecurity requirements and implementation in accordance with the JSIG and governing policy.
You will advise CISSM, CISSEs, and CISO of changes affecting the organization's cybersecurity posture.

You will be responsible for the development of Assessment and Authorization artifacts such Concept of Operation (CONOPS), System Security Plan, (SSPs), Security Controls Traceability Matrix (SCTM), System Profiles, testing documentation, and more.
You will review and evaluate the security impacts of new systems or system changes to include existing or proposed interfaces with other IT systems.
You will perform activities and prepare documentation at each step of the Risk Management Framework (RMF) in pursuit of or to maintain an Authorization to Operate (ATO).
You will perform and track Information System (IS) self-inspections, reports, system tests and responses.
You will analyze vulnerability scans, STIG compliance and deficiencies of all types identified during internal and external cyber security reviews.
You will ensure that deficiencies and vulnerabilities are included in a Plan of Action and Milestones and are tracked until the adequate mitigation measures have been implemented.
You will perform data integrity containments and investigations on Information Assurance (IA) related security violations / incidents.
You will manage and mentor assigned CSWF members.
You will conduct security education training for system users and peers on appropriate risk mitigation strategies and security practices on an initial and annual basis.
Details.Education: In lieu of specialized experience you may qualify with the following education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree

MajorDuties: You will coach and lead a team through Agile ceremonies: Daily Stand-Ups; Iteration/Sprint Reviews, Retrospectives, Planning events and Backlog Refinement.
You will assist the team with preparation and execution of demonstrations, increment and iteration/sprint planning.
You will work with team members to identify risks, analyze risks and derive mitigation steps.
You will assist the team with story/task writing and pointing, including acceptance criteria and enabler stories.
You will engage in pre-planning to prepare for planning events.
You will collaborate with other scrum masters and teams to reach program objectives and facilitate coordination of dependencies.
You will use appropriate Agile technical tools, e.g., Jira and Confluence, and work products, e.g., burndown chart, to track Sprint progress and achieve team increment goals.
You will monitor and keep the team on track during sprints, increments and planning sessions.
You will help remove internal and external impediments to team progress.
You will facilitate team and individual member development and decision making through mentoring and coaching to foster team self-organization and self-governance.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: For 08xx Basic Requirements: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. For 1310 Basic Requirements: A) Degree: physics; or related degree that included at least 24 semester hours in physics. OR B) Combination of education and experience -- courses equivalent to a major in physics totaling at least 24 semester hours, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In either A or B above, the courses must have included a fundamental course in general physics and, in addition, courses in any two of the following: electricity and magnetism, heat, light, mechanics, modern physics, and sound. For 1520 Basic Requirements: A) Degree: mathematics; or the equivalent of a major that included at least 24 semester hours in mathematics. OR B) Combination of education and experience -- courses equivalent to a major in mathematics (including at least 24 semester hours in mathematics), as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The total course work in either A or B above must have included differential and integral calculus and, in addition, four advanced mathematics courses requiring calculus or equivalent mathematics courses as a prerequisite. For 1550 Basic Requirements: Bachelor's degree in computer science or bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions. If you are using education to meet all or part of the qualification requirements, you must submit a copy of your transcripts or an itemized list of college courses which includes equivalent information from the transcript (course title, semester/quarter hours, and grade/degree earned) in your resume. See OPM's General Policies for information on crediting education. Education must be accredited by an accrediting institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education in order for it to be credited towards qualifications (https://www.ed.gov/). Foreign Education: Education completed in foreign colleges or universities may be used to meet the qualification requirements if the applicant can provide documentation indicating that the foreign education is comparable to that received in an accredited educational institution in the United States. It is the responsibility of the applicant to provide such evidence when applying. For further information, visit: https://www2.ed.gov/about/offices/list/ous/international/usnei/us/edlite-visitus-forrecog.html.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-09-12) or pay band (NM-03) in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector in order to perform the duties of a Supervisory Interdisciplinary Engineer/Scientist. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a Supervisory Interdisciplinary Engineer/Scientist in the Point Mugu Sea Range Department of NAVAIRWARCENWPNDIV POINT MUGU.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will ensure work within the Branch fully supports the missions of the Sea Range Support Division and the Point Mugu Sea Range Department.
You will lead professionals in the fields of project management, office management, mission assurance, physical security, business software, configuration/data management and workload metrics.
You will develop, plan and execute the Branch?s workload, which supports the business and technical operations for the Point Mugu Sea Range Department.
You will manage the technical and administrative tasks assigned to the Branch.
You will be responsible for performance management (DPMAP/STRL), recruitment and hiring, training and development, space planning and financial planning and execution.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following positive education qualifications requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: Applicants must posses 08XX Series: Successful completion of a degree in Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR A Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. 1550 Series: Bachelor's degree in computer science OR Bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will develop solutions that collect, store, manipulate, transform or present data and information by means of non-distributed and distributed computer systems.
You will develop and deploy enterprise-to-tactical information systems, including performance, business, infrastructure, application, services, and data information architecture.
You will develop conceptual and physical data models.
You will develop solutions for the representation and transformation of information structures.
You will develop Service-Oriented Architectures, portable scripts, standalone and web-based application, and prototype software products and artifacts.
You will apply mathematical, statistical, and/or data sciences to detect, classify, identify, and predict using Mission Data.
Details.Education: Applicants must meet the following basic education requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual: For 0801 series: Successful completion of a professional engineering degree. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. OR Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website at: http://www.nspe.org OR Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information, please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html. OR Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and in engineering that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A (above). The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A (above) OR Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least one year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily, there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. For 1550 Series: Bachelor's degree in computer science or bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions. For 1520 Series: A) Degree: mathematics; or the equivalent of a major that included at least 24 semester hours in mathematics. OR B) Combination of education and experience -- courses equivalent to a major in mathematics (including at least 24 semester hours in mathematics), as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The total course work in either A or B above must have included differential and integral calculus and, in addition, four advanced mathematics courses requiring calculus or equivalent mathematics courses as a prerequisite. For 1310 Series: A) Degree: physics; or related degree that included at least 24 semester hours in physics OR B) Combination of education and experience -- courses equivalent to a major in physics totaling at least 24 semester hours, plus appropriate experience or additional education. In either A or B above, the courses must have included a fundamental course in general physics and, in addition, courses in any two of the following: electricity and magnetism, heat, light, mechanics, modern physics, and sound.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate one year of information technology related experience in the federal service or private or public sector demonstrating the following four competencies, as defined: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Verifying all processes, security features, and configurations are unaltered. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Providing support and cross-support to various cybersecurity and system administrators. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Communicating with software developers, users, and other personnel as needed to resolve issues resulting from patching, upgrades, or other sustainment/development activities. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Researching, analyzing impact, installing, and testing software updates, patches and hot fixes. (GS-12): In addition to experience demonstrating the four competencies above, your resume must demonstrate one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-11) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience includes duties related to the following: 1) Applying expertise in Linux and Windows operating systems configuration and management to execute IT programs and system modifications; 2) Introducing new technologies and/or methodologies into current or proposed systems to address organizational requirements; 3) Collaborating closely with supervisors, IT Specialists, and cybersecurity (CS) personnel to address IT-related matters related to planning, programming, development, modification, and adherence to IT systems policies and procedures; 4) Implementing corrective measures for immediate issues and implementing preventative measures to mitigate future occurrences. (GS-11): In addition to experience demonstrating the four competencies above, your resume must demonstrate one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-09) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience includes duties related to the following: 1) Managing the installation, testing, operation, troubleshooting, and maintenance of both hardware and software systems, encompassing routers, switches, workstations, and servers; 2) Evaluating costs and various considerations to suggest appropriate system products, diagnostic tools, and upgrades, aligning with present and future requirements; 3) Demonstrating customer service abilities by devising performance measures, closely monitoring achievements, reporting on performance, and promptly responding to data requests. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will be the Team Lead in the Combat Systems Test and Evaluation Department to support multiple programs and combat system elements.

You will provide leadership of the Database Architecture (OBA) team, and programs planning, executing, preparing, reviewing, and evaluating technology solutions in support of new systems acquisition or sustainment programs.
You will provide technological solutions of operational readiness in support of improving Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) of Combat systems.
You will lead personnel with a variety of technology expertise in developing and implementing programmatic requirements from acquisition through phase out.
You will design and develop new technology solutions for process automation and process improvement.

You will and analyze and gathering project requirements by partnering with key stakeholders across the organization to provide technology solutions that help the organization operated more efficiently and cost-effectively.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or related field AND at least three years of progressive technical experience as Business Analyst, Systems Analyst, Programmer Analyst or Database Administrator in the retail, supply chain or financial industry OR an appropriate combination of education and experience that demonstrates possession of knowledge and skill equivalent to that gained in the above OR appropriate experience that demonstrates that the applicant has acquired the knowledge and skills and abilities equivalent to that gained above. Key skills for the position: Ability to understand and develop creative processes and system solutions. Experience using MS-Visio and/or Erwin. Knowledge of UML/BPMN modeling tools. Ability to create data models from requirements. Ability to create and manage project plans using Microsoft MS-Project. Ability to work with Project Managers creating project documents and tracking project changes. Experience collecting requirements for definition, design, testing, and implementation of IT systems. Ability to create System Requirements Specifications (SRS) documentation. Ability to utilize software to create test scripts and track systems defects. Validates and tests developed solutions. Knowledge and experience using basic SQL commands. Knowledge of Data Warehouse concepts (Star/Snowflake schemas) and the ETL process. Knowledge of at least one object-oriented development languages (C#.Net, Python, R), APIs, JSON/REST, and Docker. Knowledge of SOLID principles. Experience with Cybersecurity requirements (STIG, IL 4 and above, and ATO process). Ability to manage changes in the requirements and participate in the Change Management process. Ability to manage the Business Intelligence (BI) team tasks queue. Must possess excellent analytical, logic, and presentation skills. Must possess effective verbal and written communication skills. Ability to use Microsoft Office 365 suite of applications. This position has been designated as a position of trust. The incumbent must be eligible for an Access National Agency Check and Inquiries (ANACI/ Tier 3) background investigation to satisfy IT Level II designation. Appointment and continued employment are subject to a favorable adjudication of the security investigation. Eligible for incremental telework as determined by MR/MF policy.

Details.JobSummary: Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) is looking for the best and brightest to join our Team! MCCS is a comprehensive program that supports and enhances the quality of life for Marines, their families, and others in the Marine Corps Community. We offer a team oriented environment comprised of military personnel, civilian employees, contractors and volunteers who keep the organization functioning smoothly and effectively.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Serving Those Who Serve
MajorDuties: Serves as Business Analyst – The Business Intelligence Business Analyst is responsible for collecting and discussing requirements using elicitation techniques with key stakeholders. Uses business process modelling tools e.g., UML, BPMN, user stories, etc. to model and document MCCS processes. Creates data models from requirements and System Requirements Specifications (SRS) documentation, Manages changes in the requirements. Validates and tests developed solutions, Works with Project Managers to create project documents and track project changes. Coordinates User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and applications rollout into production. Manages the Business Intelligence (BI) team tasks queue. Helps creating ad-hoc and on-demand reports using SQL, Cognos, and other tools. Supports the development of data analytics dashboards, reports, and data warehouse. Leads the development of project scope and objectives. Consults with personnel or organization units involved to analyze current operational procedures, identify problems, and learn specific input and output requirements. Research industry systems and technology utilized outside the organization that may be possible system solutions for the business. Analyzes and challenges user requests by finding alternative innovative solutions. Participates in the development of project plans. Documents detailed description of user needs, program functions, and steps required to develop or modify computer systems. Creates process flow diagrams to specify current and future business processes for review by business areas and development teams. Maintains and supports changes to the functional specifications document throughout the project. Serves as liaison to internal or external development team(s) in resolution of functional specification issues, business process flow, testing, and implementation requirements. Leads in the preparation and facilitation of joint application development sessions. Schedules user requirements and review meetings. Prepares agenda and presentations for meetings. Documents and distributes meeting minutes. Presents screen prototypes of design to business community. Provides functional specifications document to development staff during a Technical Review. Demonstrates to users how proposed system solution will support their business needs and secures their acceptance and signoff of the functional specifications document. Communicates updates/enhancements made to the system post implementation to the business user community. Prepares status reports indicating accomplishments and next steps for the reporting period as well as identifying any project related issues. Participates in weekly meetings with project team to discuss any project related matters as well as providing business related information. Reviews computer system capabilities, workflow, and scheduling limitations to determine if requested change is necessary and conforms to MCCS objectives. Responsible for maintaining project scope and objective by not allowing scope creep. Evaluates business user need in comparison to development effort and cost to determine appropriate course of action that minimized risk. Develops and documents a test plan, test cases, and expected results based on the functional specifications document. Compiles test data that will execute each test case. Coordinates with the development team to execute system test in accordance with the test plan. Evaluates the testing output against the expected results documented in the test plan. Documents system flaws. Communicates necessary fixes to development team. Re-execute test scenarios to ensure desired results are met. Supports Quality Assurance team in final testing phase prior to implementation. Collaborates system testing with the user community for their evaluation and acceptance. Prioritizes system fixes/changes/installation based on severity to normal business interruptions. Ensures that the agreed to system solution is understood by the user community and is integrated into their business procedures. Assists users in development of business process and timeline documentation. Formulates job aides to assist in the implementation of new business procedures. Coordinates the creation of user manuals with the training department. Responsible for initial training of core business users. Provides post implementation support and necessary follow-up training.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field appropriate to the work, or an appropriate combination of education and experience that demonstrates that the applicant has acquired the necessary knowledge, skills, and experiences to operate effectively in this senior technical position. Six years of progressive experience as a PeopleSoft Developer, which includes researching, designing, developing, migrating and testing PeopleSoft HCM. Demonstrated experience leading Enterprise PeopleSoft development and support. Expert knowledge of; PeopleCode, PeopleTools, Workflow, Application Engine, Component Interface, Integration Broker. Expert knowledge of at least two of the reporting tools (PS Query, Tree Manager, PS/nVision, SQR, XML Publisher). Expert knowledge of one or more PeopleSoft application modules and integration between modules. Working knowledge of the PeopleSoft Internet Architecture, PeopleTools 8.50 and above, WebLogic and Tuxedo. Expertise in retrofitting customized objects (components, pages, fields, records, modified PeopleCode, etc.). Ability to debug complex PeopleCode and Application Engine programs. Experience with Oracle SQL required. Knowledge of Infrastructure & configuration of Application Server, Web Server and Process Scheduler as related to PeopleSoft is required. Proficiency in maintaining all aspects of cybersecurity and compliance including Risk Management Framework (RMF), NIST 800-53 requirements and best practices. Expert knowledge and experience in implementing STIGs on applicable software, running and remediating IT security vulnerability scans, investigating cyber security events and assisting with remediation guidance, administration of fixes, updates and enhancements. Demonstrated experience with networking concepts to include subnetting and network devices (such as firewalls, routers, and switches, log monitoring and auditing) and in conducting risk management assessments to identify relevant threats to security, vulnerabilities, and the potential for exploiting those vulnerabilities. Must be detail oriented and team player. Strong analytical skills required. Eagerness to mentor junior staff. Must be able to work independently and manage multiple tasks. Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills. Experience with both UNIX and Windows Server environments. Strong oral and written communication. Requirements collection, requirements analysis, solution analysis, design, development, coding, testing, implementation, maintenance and documentation for the PeopleSoft Human Capital Management System (HCM) suite.

MajorDuties: The Section Head, Database Services is responsible for leading the Database Administration Section within Infrastructure and Enterprise Services Branch, Chief Information Officer (CIO). Leads a team of Database Administrators to establish, support and maintain all databases for all business and support software systems and web solutions provided for worldwide operations within Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS). Databases being maintained may be in a government owned/leased data center, in the cloud, or a hybrid environment and primarily include Oracle and SQL Server. Leads the administration of Oracle Databases for the administration and development of the MCCS Informatica Data Warehouse/Lake/Hub environments. Roles Include: • Leads the Databases Services section: government, contractor, and 3rd party personnel. • Performs complex design, development, and deployment of multiple database solutions for a variety of system architectures. • Performs physical and logical data modeling, creation, normalization, loading, performance tuning, cybersecurity, and monitoring of databases. • Manages and ensures availability, reliability, and security of all data and metadata throughout life cycles of all software systems. • Leads efforts to install, upgrade, patch, configure, tune, test, document, backup, and recover databases. • Develops long range plans to meet MCCS Enterprise IT strategic and budget objectives in support of MCCS business and mission outcomes. • Coordinates with IT Management and collaborates with other IT teams (e.g., Network services, Systems Administration, Cybersecurity, Help Desk, Project Management, Web services, and Application services) and business functions as appropriate. • Secures database servers and databases in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) guidelines. • Works with Cybersecurity and application owners to conduct assessment and authorization activities in support of Risk Management Framework compliance. • Documents and implements Database server/Database STIGs controls, Standard operating procedure (SOP) and configuration documents. • Performs data and business process analysis in support of CIO process improvement activities. • Evaluates third party software to determine if it will meet business and operational needs and is compatible with existing operating systems and applications. • Participates in budget planning for IT projects and IT operations: IT Capital & IT Operations and Maintenance (O&M). Supervises full performance employees to include: assigning and distributing work, coaching, counseling, tutoring, and mentoring employees; approving and disapproving leave, recommending and completing personnel actions, completing performance reviews and signing timecards, training employees, awarding performance awards and disciplinary actions, keeping abreast of and actively supporting the principles of the EEO program, and prevention of sexual harassment. Must be alert to alcohol abuse and take appropriate action. This is a white-collar position where occasional lifting up to 20 lbs may be required.

MajorDuties: All U.S. Citizens who reside or currently employed in the MCB Quantico local commuting area, which includes the Virginia counties of Albemarle, Arlington, Caroline, Chesterfield, Culpeper, Fairfax, Fauquier, Greene, Hanover, Henrico, King George, Loudoun, Louisa, Madison, Orange, Prince William, Spotsylvania and Stafford Counties, and the cities of Alexandria, Fairfax, Fredericksburg, Manassas, Manassas Park, and Richmond; Maryland counties of Anne Arundel, Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's and Saint Mary's; District of Columbia; and all cities existing in Virginia or Maryland within the geographic area bounded by the outer boundaries of the combined areas of the aforementioned counties. As a SUPERVISORY IT SPECIALIST (PRINCIPAL DEPUTY) you will be responsible for the following duties: As the Principal Deputy Chief Information Officer (PDCIO) incumbent is responsible for full spectrum operations of a dynamic IT network providing detailed assessments, analysis, and recommendations on systems engineering, systems analysis, user experience, customer support, policy, governance, network security, and program management. Coordinates with National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST), Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), National Security Agency (NSA), Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), Joint Forces Headquarters DOD IN and others relative to information technology and cyber security policies and procedures affecting DCSA automation initiatives. Through subordinate leaders, provide technical IT engineering support including design, architecture, development, integration, assessment and authorization, oversight, and support for DCSA.

Specialized experience for this position includes: Providing assessments and technical advice on acquisition, contracting, and the budgeting processes. Providing administration and acquisitions for IT areas such as hardware, software, products and services, systems development, infrastructure design, and engineering architecture. Handling multiple contracts/task orders. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: 1. Interpersonal Skills 2. Customer Support 3. Project Management 4. Strategic Thinking

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) is a separate Agency of the Department of Defense (DoD) under the direction, authority, and control of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security (USD (I&S). MajorDuties: As a SUPERVISORY IT SPECIALIST you will be responsible for the following duties: Provide expert technical and managerial support to OCIO IT Enterprise Operations to maintain operations, upgrade and optimize service delivery. Serve as a supervisory IT Specialist at the Branch level providing leadership, technical oversight, service operations direction and customer support to the DCSA workforce. Provide operational liaison between the government, DoD, and commercial service providers to ensure enterprise IT operations. Maintains contact with technical and customer service representatives to plan and coordinate work, ensure are up to date with system design, and resolve operational problems. Maintains effective relationships with upper-level management, system administrators, and commercial vendors to stay abreast of improvements and advances in information technology and service delivery models. Assign work to subordinates based on priorities, selective consideration of the difficulty and requirements of assignments, and the capabilities of employees; Evaluating work performance of subordinates; Giving advice, counsel, or instruction to employees on both work and administrative matters. Direct or participate in complex projects and provides expert technical assistance to maximize the utilization of technology to attain economies and productivity for agency. Develop specifications for proposals for the procurement of new and/or revised information technology systems. Develops new concepts in cost avoidance modeling to provide the most cost-effective services. Conducts studies and comparative analyses to assess the effectiveness of programs implementation. Makes recommendations based on findings and presents to upper-level management. Review and evaluate proposals for technical accuracy and fulfillment of requirements. Participates in the operational testing of acquired systems of prior to their acceptance by the agency. Evaluates the potential of new products and improvements in terms of improved service and economy in meeting user needs.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, there is no Group Coverage Qualification Standard for this series. BASIC REQUIREMENT OR INDIVIDUAL OCCUPATIONAL REQUIREMENT: Through experience in Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations AND SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes making decisions and initiates actions that involve interpretation of policy or the setting of precedents; authoritative determinations and advises on complex, never-before-solved technical problems and applications of technology. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of IT infrastructure development and management, systems integration, IT acquisition and vendor management, IT lifecycle management, and hardware and software development, maintenance, and sustainment sufficient to organize the research of development of and adoption of technical standards and solutions that promote the insertion of new technologies. Knowledge of modern software project management techniques and concepts, to include agile methodologies, the requirements gathering/user story development processes, with the ability to provide expert technical advice and guidance to senior leadership on appropriate programmatic decisions and applications of technology that can meet current and future mission requirements. Knowledge of a wide range of computer programming languages and modern software frameworks such as Angular, Python, Java, XML-based metadata generation, the handling, transformation, programing for common internet protocols (HTTP, HTTTPS, FTP), interfacing software with SQL databases; and JavaScript libraries (jQuery, ExtJS), PHP programing, SQL database administration/manipulation, cross domain application level security guards/gateways, implementation of Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and vulnerability assessment tools. Knowledge of DoD policies related to the protection of classified information as it pertains to information technology systems, including the specialized policy requirements of Special Access Programs and their associated Security Classification Guides, along with the Authorization to operate approval process. Skilled in oral communications with the ability to present information and/or recommendations on complex matters to higher authorities; skilled in written communications sufficient to develop guidance, regulations and directives dealing with complex issues and maintain good working relations. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and staff of a small to medium sized organization. Ability to gather, assemble, and analyze facts, draw conclusions, conduct analysis, devise recommended solutions, and package the entire process in briefings, papers, or reports suitable for top management use and decision-making. Ability to establish and maintain highly productive working relationships with team members, clients, industry experts, and others including interpersonal effectiveness with executive management, peers, employees, and contractors as well as in building relationships and maintaining close coordination with a range of customers. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: This vacancy is being re-announced. Candidates who applied for Announcement # 9L-AFPC-12108939-138241-DPW must self-nominate for this Announcement in order to receive consideration. Please remember to re-submit all applicable supporting documents. Please be advised, if you have missing supporting documents or the documents are incomplete, you will not be eligible for the chosen appointment. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. GS-11 SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes in a developmental capacity knowledge of legal research methods; classification and declassification procedures for DoD information within the guidelines established by the appropriate Executive Orders. Requires detail oriented analytical ability for reviewing historical and current information to determine its sensitivity. Knowledge of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Privacy Act (PA) to include the computer matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988. OR EDUCATION: Successfully completed a Ph.D or equivalent graduate degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position. NOTE: You must submit copies of your college transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: I have a combination of specialized experience and education. A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts. GS-12 SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-11, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes knowledge of legal research methods; classification and declassification procedures for DoD information within the guidelines established by the appropriate Executive Orders. Requires detail oriented analytical ability for reviewing historical and current information to determine its sensitivity. As well, knowledge of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Privacy Act (PA) to include the computer matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. One year at the GS-11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-12 level. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Privacy Act (PA) to include the computer matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988, recent judicial decisions affecting the FOIA and PA policy of the Department of Justice, DOD Directives, and Secretary of the Air Force and AFOSI FOIA regulations. 2. Knowledge of the laws, regulations, and decisions applicable to FOIA and PA; skill in the application of Federal and public laws, DoD, regulatory requirements, principles, concepts and methodologies. 3. Knowledge of electronic FOIA tools/databases/programs and software (such as Redact Xpress and eFOIA) used for document, video, and audio redactions. 4. Skill in performing research and applying analytical and evaluative techniques for the identification, consideration, resolution of issues or problems and responding to requests concerning FOIA/PA and AFOSI records. 5. Ability to develop new or revised policies and modify existing procedures and instructions pertaining to the administration and implementation of the FOIA and PA programs. 6. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing. Ability to work independently and with minimal supervision and guidance and as a part of a team. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Additional Conditions of Employment: This position has been designated by the Air Force as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the Air Force Civilian Drug Demand Reduction program. Employee must pass initial and periodic short notice drug testing. Illegal drug use by employees is sensitive positions presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security and public safety.

MajorDuties: GS-12 The primary purpose of this position is to provide timely, accurate, relevant and authoritative legal responses on request for disclosure of sensitive investigative information, that involve law enforcement criminal case files, counter-intelligence and/or intelligence case files and other source documents. Duties: Reviews, analyses, substantiates, and processes requests for disclosure of AFOSI information, to include all Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Privacy Act (PA) requests with assistance when needed on unique requests from the Initial Denial Signatory or the Staff Judge Advocated. Exercises responsibility to keep current with new developments and recent court decisions, legislative activities, and congressional initiatives regarding release of information under the FOIA (including legal interpretation and decision) Privacy Act Laws, Civil Liberty Laws, and other pertinent laws, Executive orders and precedents pertaining to information disclosures, security and protection of information. Employs extensive knowledge of all AFOSI records systems, internal procedures, and investigative methodologies to determine if records requested are complete when received from other AFOSI offices. Utilizes internal and external contacts to confer or determine and clarify requested information.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Domestic Defense Industrial Base/Major Range and Test Facilities Base Civilian Personnel Workforce Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the Basic Education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Education Requirement for Engineering - 0800 series: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program. 4. Related Curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in engineering technology or in an appropriate professional field, e.g., physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. (You MUST submit a copy of your transcripts along with a letter of reference stating that you have at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. The letter must be signed by the engineer who provided the professional engineer supervision. It must also include their name, phone number, and list their engineer credentials such as engineer education or professional certificates). Basic Education Requirement for Physical Scientist - 1301 series: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to a major in physics totaling at least 24 semester hours, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The courses must have included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. Basic Education Requirement for Computer Scientist - 1550 series: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in computer science or bachelor's degree (or higher degree) with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. Basic Requirement for Data Scientist Series-1501 series: A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in mathematics, statistics, or actuarial science. The degree must be in a major field of study (at least at the baccalaureate level) that is appropriate for the position. OR B. Combination of Education and Experience: Courses equivalent to a major field of study as shown in paragraph A above, plus additional education or appropriate experience. In addition to meeting one of the basic requirements above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the Specialized Experience requirements listed below: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Expertise planning or coordinating tests of weapon systems; 2) Expertise coordinating personnel, test facilities or resources to support scheduled test missions; and 3) Experience utilizing knowledge of Test and Evaluation principals, practices, methods, and techniques. The definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (NH-03 or GS-13). You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Decision Making Leadership Project Management Technical Requirements Management Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-13).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves under the Commander of a Major Test and Evaluation (T&E) Facility (Test Center/Proving Ground) under the Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC). Responsible to the Commander for the technical control, coordination and management of the facility's programs with maximum delegation of technical and administrative management matters. Management may select at any series announced.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Serves as Technical Director and is responsible to the Commander for accomplishment of the total mission and the effective and economic internal functioning of the organization
Responsible to the Commander for the technical control, coordination and management of the command programs with maximum delegations of technical and administrative management matters.
Provides direction, guidance, oversight, and supervision for all activities of the command
Manages program planning for life cycle test and evaluation of weapons systems, i.e., aviation, aviation systems, missiles, and sensors
Recommend broad policies to the Commander and institutes procedures which will ensure mission accomplishment.
Directs strategic planning to ensure test capabilities are ready and relevant to support scheduled tests.
Assures professional development of test personnel to become subject matter experts in their respective fields
Advances testing methodology and technology plans, studies, programs and policies to efficiently and effectively test complex weapon system technologies.
Maintains viable safety, environmental and security programs and complies with governing policies and regulations
Oversees the management of resources, schedules, and budgets in all phases of operations

Participates and represents the organization in conferences/meetings that requires extensive preparation to exchange information, evaluate/coordinate projects, defend actions, and propose controversial solutions.
Works with management to establish new fundamental concepts and criteria and stimulate the development of new policies, methodologies, and techniques.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Computer Engineering (0854)/Electronics Engineering (0855): A. Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET); OR (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. ORB. Combination of Education and Experience: College-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following:1. Professional registration or licensure - Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT), or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) examination, or any other written test required for professional registration, by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in A above. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program. 4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. Basic Requirement for Computer Science (1550): Degree: Bachelor's degree (or higher degree) in computer science or bachelor's degree (or higher degree) with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: To qualify based on your work experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience which prepared you to do the work in this job. Specialized experience is defined as experience that is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled such as 1) Providing analytical technical advice in matters relating to information management issues (telecommunications, cyber security, info tech/operational tech architecture); 2) Establishing operational requirements utilizing multiple engineering or computer science disciplines associated with information technology; 3) Carrying out strategies/actions to affirm the integrity, economy, quality, and effectiveness of engineering architecture or scientific programs; 4) Observing progress to advice on engineering/computer science inadequacies leading to organizational concerns. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-13). You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Communications Information Management Information Technology Architecture Problem Solving Technology Management Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience and education--no substitution of education for experience is permitted you must have both.
